disease_label_per_paper: Disseminated Histoplasmosis with Secondary Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis in a Renal Transplant Recipient on Belatacept-based Immunosuppression
presentation_summary: 62-year-old woman presented with fever, shortness of breath, chills, and myalgia 18 months after deceased-donor renal transplant for ESRD from focal segmental glomerulosclerosis.
She was receiving mycophenolate, belatacept, and prednisone, with last belatacept infusion nine days before admission.

Presentation showed fever 100.8 F, tachycardia 102/min, tachypnea 32/min, toxic appearance, moderate distress, bilateral fine crackles, acute hypoxic respiratory failure, elevated procalcitonin, high LDH, transaminitis, anemia, and renal dysfunction.

Chest X-ray showed cardiomegaly with bilateral pulmonary infiltrates; respiratory status worsened despite antibiotics, diuresis, systemic steroids, and non-invasive ventilation, requiring ICU transfer and later mechanical ventilation.

BAL and urine culture plus BAL PCR confirmed Histoplasma; peripheral smear showed intracellular yeast; she developed secondary HLH with ferritin >15,000, fibrinogen 87 mg/dL, triglycerides 1000 mg/dL, LDH >12,650, severe transaminitis, encephalopathy, and pancytopenia, and died despite maximal therapy.

quality_warnings: Histoplasma BAL/urine culture, BAL PCR, and peripheral smear fungal identification are stored under confirmatory_findings, not ordinary observations.
Two-week HLH values are stored in lab_trajectories/course_observations rather than initial snapshot observations.
No initial blood pressure or oxygen saturation value was reported; respiratory severity is represented by respiratory rate, acute hypoxic respiratory failure, oxygen support level, and imaging.
MRI/EEG abnormalities are neurologic complications in the course; the article does not prove CNS histoplasmosis specifically.
